grafs: Financial Stability Board Chair Andrew Bailey, in a letter dated 28 August 2026 and published for the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors meetings on 31 August and 1 September, warned that frontier AI models are “showing increasingly sophisticated autonomy and problem-solving abilities, as well as threat capabilities.” For the financial system, he wrote, “the most immediate concern is the potential impact of frontier AI on cyber risk.”

“Frontier AI may have the ability materially to alter the speed, scale and economics of cyber risk, which could undermine market confidence system-wide, especially due to highly concentrated third-party service providers,” Bailey wrote. He urged firms to prepare for simultaneous disruption across multiple firms or shared technology dependencies, including the ability to restore critical systems and data from “bare metal,” and said many jurisdictions still lack protocols for safe frontier-model release and deployment.

Outside the AI section, Bailey said markets remain vulnerable to a potentially disorderly correction given fragilities in sovereign debt, vulnerabilities in private credit, and stretched asset valuations — “particularly artificial intelligence-related investments.” He also flagged leverage in equity markets interacting with high valuations and market concentration, “in particular the increasing cross-investment between artificial intelligence (AI) companies and hyper scalers.” The letter is a chair warning, not a new FSB rule or quantified loss scenario.

grafs: SLB (NYSE: SLB) announced Aug. 31 it has signed an agreement to acquire Kelvion, a global provider of thermal management and heat exchange technologies, from Apollo-managed funds — the majority owner — and funds advised by Triton, which holds a minority interest. Under the terms, SLB will pay approximately $3.4 billion in cash and assume approximately $0.7 billion of debt. Apollo’s matching release headlines the sale at $4.1 billion. SLB says that consideration represents a total transaction value of approximately 11 times estimated 2026 EBITDA before synergies, or approximately 8.5 times EBITDA including expected annual run-rate synergies. Official: SLB newsroom PR-2026-0831; Apollo press page, Aug. 31.

Kelvion is expected in 2026 to generate revenue of approximately $2.3 billion to $2.4 billion and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $350 million to $400 million, SLB said. Data centers are its largest and fastest-growing end market: about 55 percent of 2026 revenue, or $1.2 billion to $1.3 billion, and more than 50 percent growth from 2025. Official prepared remarks: Kelvion first-half 2026 bookings were $1.5 billion, up 43 percent year over year. Combined SLB and Kelvion data-center bookings in the first half of 2026 rose more than 130 percent versus the first half of 2025, for a combined book-to-bill of 1.8 times. On a 2026 pro-forma basis the two data-center businesses are expected to generate more than $2 billion in revenue and approximately $300 million in adjusted EBITDA; SLB is targeting $4.5 billion to $5 billion of revenue and $700 million to $800 million of adjusted EBITDA for the combined data-center solutions business in 2028. SLB’s existing Data Center Solutions business is on track to exit 2027 at an annualized revenue run-rate exceeding $2 billion, with delivered capacity expected to surpass 2 gigawatts cumulatively by year-end 2026.

CFO Stephane Biguet, in the prepared remarks: the deal will be financed with existing cash and debt; leverage stays inside the previously stated through-cycle target of up to 1.5 times net debt-to-EBITDA. Annual EBITDA synergies of approximately $120 million within three years, with about 60 percent in the second year; approximately $70 million of that stack is cost. Accretive to EPS and free cash flow per share in the first 12 months after close. Shareholder returns: more than $4 billion in 2026 between dividends and buybacks is reaffirmed, and $4 billion is now a floor for 2027. Close remains the first half of 2027. Olivier Le Peuch said SLB will serve as the modular design partner for NVIDIA DSX AI factories — that is an SLB remarks line, not a NVIDIA Newsroom post. Official IR Q&A transcript (LSEG StreetEvents, posted to investorcenter.slb.com): Biguet said the 2028 $4.5 billion to $5 billion revenue target “does not include Kelvion’s so-called diversified industrial business, the non-data center… that is data center only.” CapEx is 2 to 3 percent of revenue, currently closer to 3 percent as Kelvion adds capacity, with steady state closer to 2 percent. “Currently, the margins are not accretive to the overall SLB business.” Combined first-half 2026 book-to-bill of 1.8 times converts to revenue in about six to nine months; the 2028 range is either already in backlog or awarded with volumes committed, with purchase orders issued gradually by hyperscalers. Of the $120 million synergy stack, $50 million is revenue, with cost synergies first. Do not write a $4.1 billion enterprise-value gloss that is not in the SLB release; pair Apollo’s $4.1 billion headline with the $3.4 billion cash / $0.7 billion debt split both companies print.

grafs: The Wall Street Journal reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter, that Nvidia has paused some deals in a financing initiative that offered credit support to AI cloud companies in exchange for a share of revenue. The company stepped back from the program last week, the Journal said, and could still revamp the initiative or fold it into another program. WSJ exclusive timestamp: Aug. 27, 5:46 p.m. ET. Reuters recaps: CNA and The Straits Times.

An Nvidia spokesperson told Reuters: “The new business model … that opens up compute access to the fast-growing AI ecosystem is still in place and continues to evolve due to high demand.” Do not write that Nvidia killed the program. The 50 percent take above a threshold is the Journal’s account of proposed deals, from people familiar — not a number Nvidia has published.

On Wednesday’s FQ2 call (official IR transcript, FactSet CallStreet), Nvidia described the structure in its own words: a take-or-pay commitment on a portion of a facility’s capacity — “a minimum revenue guarantee that gives lenders the confidence to underwrite the project” — and, in exchange, a share of the neocloud’s revenue earned above that floor. “We’re not making loans.” “In this model, we get paid twice, once on the hardware sale and again through the share of rental revenue,” with “the potential to drive billions in revenue over the medium to long term.” Independent capital still underwrites every deal on its own merits, the company said.

The Journal reported that some Nvidia employees expressed concerns to current and potential customers that the initiative could draw antitrust scrutiny, and that there are sensitivities around how far Nvidia can dictate how customers do business. Nvidia told some cloud providers they could rent its chips out only to approved customers and signaled it preferred capacity be distributed among multiple smaller firms rather than one large customer, the report said. Investor circular-deal scrutiny is the backdrop; do not collapse this pause with the signed $105 billion Ohio LPS cap or the preliminary >$500 billion financing MOUs already on this plate. The July blog named Sharon AI and Firmus as among the first companies on the model — the WSJ recap does not say those specific deals were paused, so do not write that.

stories.hed: Your AI, On a Dial
stories.dek: Park et al. arXiv 2608.22852. Tuesday mailing. One MLP neuron steers buy/sell on five open-weight models. Closed models out of scope. Not a product lever.

grafs: Sahong Park and co-authors posted “Your AI, On a Dial: Controlling Investment Bias in LLMs with a Single Neuron” to the Tuesday arXiv mailing (2608.22852; cs.AI, cross-list q-fin). The intervention is one MLP neuron at inference time. It shifts a model-level buy/sell prior without changing the prompt or the weights, and without targeting particular firms. The tests are five open-weight models: Qwen3-8B, Llama-4-Scout, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, Gemma-4-12B-it and Mistral-Small-24B.

Across those five, the dial produces monotonic changes in investment stance. Under identical inputs it also shifts the evidential emphasis of the generated rationales, and in an agentic retrieval setting it changes what the model searches for, which evidence it opens, and what lands in the memo. In long context the dial holds while a matched system-prompt instruction attenuates. An exploratory weekly-news backtest moves rankings and portfolio composition; the authors flag it as not investment alpha.

Closed models are out of scope. The method needs access to internal activations, which we do not have. Forge confirmed there is no activation access here. Treat the paper as a research note, not a product lever.

stories.hed: Do not treat the LLM label as the construct
stories.dek: Dell and Rambachan. arXiv 2608.23524. NBER methods lecture. Rubric, random validation sample, de-bias. Prompt and model search can flip the sign.
stories.action: Do not ship an LLM-labeled series as the construct. Rubric, random validation sample, de-bias. Prompt/model search can flip the sign.
grafs: Melissa Dell and Ashesh Rambachan posted “The Measurement Revolution? Credible Measurement and Inference in the Age of AI” to arXiv (2608.23524), accompanying the NBER 2026 Methods Lecture on estimation and inference with AI-generated data. AI makes it cheap to turn text and images into structured variables. The bottleneck, they argue, is no longer finding any scalable measure of a phenomenon; it is choosing among many that can support different conclusions.

Do not treat LLM labels as the construct. A rubric does not pin down the model, the prompt, or the settings. Ludwig, Mullainathan and Rambachan (2026) document that varying the language model and the prompt can move estimates in magnitude, in statistical significance, and in sign. Baumann and co-authors (2025), replicating 21 published annotation tasks, show that a handful of prompt paraphrases can make virtually any hypothesis appear statistically significant.

The route they defend is validation, not proxy talk: write an explicit rubric, label a random validation sample, and de-bias the downstream estimate. Prediction errors are learned from that design even if the model is arbitrarily biased. Agreement across models is weaker evidence than it looks — frontier systems share architectures and training data. When a random validation sample is unavailable, identification rests on assumptions about how the models err, which have to be stated.

stories.hed: KellyBoost: growth wins the loss, not the book
stories.dek: Li. arXiv 2608.23393. Exact Kelly loss on multi-output XGBoost. Growth beats the classification surrogate. Full-Kelly concentrates and loses to predict-then-optimize.
stories.action: Keep the 2×2: growth beats the surrogate. Do not write full-Kelly as a win over predict-then-optimize. No public GitHub.
grafs: Jiayu Li posted “KellyBoost: Growth-Optimal Portfolio Construction with Gradient-Boosted Trees” to arXiv (2608.23393). End-to-end portfolio learning — map features straight to weights under a financial objective, with no intermediate return forecast — had required backpropagation, which shut out gradient-boosted trees. KellyBoost is a single multi-output XGBoost whose softmax is the portfolio and whose training loss is −log(1 + w⊤y), the exact Kelly growth objective, not a surrogate.

On a 23-year, eight-asset public-data testbed under a separated selection/estimation protocol, a 2×2 of {boosted tree, MLP} × {growth objective, classification surrogate} finds the growth objective improves deployed log growth over the surrogate within both learner classes, in both of two independently built feature pipelines: four of four cells. Because the growth objective also trades less in every cell, transaction costs widen the gap rather than eroding it.

The same testbed prices the boundary. Faithfully optimizing an estimated conditional full-Kelly allocation concentrates aggressively, and in this regime the end-to-end learners trail the classic two-stage predict-then-optimize pipeline, whose squared-error forecasts shrink toward zero and whose optimizer therefore holds milder books. The paper does not list a public GitHub; do not invent one.

stories.hed: Arbitrage-aware latent diffusion for IV surface paths
stories.dek: Buchegger and Gonon, St. Gallen. arXiv 2608.22478. Joint 30-step IVS–return trajectories. Pair with Hashimoto et al. 2608.20842, already on this paper.
stories.action: Pair with 2608.20842: score generators on the compatibility gap, not smile RMSE. Persistence still wins the one-day point forecast.
grafs: Dominik Manuel Buchegger and Lukas Gonon of the University of St. Gallen posted “Arbitrage-Aware Multi-Step Forecasting of Implied Volatility Surfaces” to arXiv (2608.22478). A conditional latent diffusion framework generates joint 30-step trajectories of implied volatility surfaces and underlying returns. An arbitrage-aware autoencoder learns a low-dimensional surface representation; the diffusion model then captures the conditional joint evolution. Admissibility is regularised into the reconstruction map rather than patched on afterwards.

Evaluated on SPX surfaces, the model generates realistic probabilistic multi-step scenarios and also outperforms the persistence benchmark in point forecasting from about weekly horizons onward. Persistence remains superior at one day. The principal limitation is underdispersion: predictive intervals widen with the horizon but stay too narrow. Generated surfaces remain essentially free of static arbitrage.

Read it next to Hashimoto, Hirano, Ozaki and Imajo (2608.20842), already on this paper: the hedging test is whether a strategy trained on synthetic paths still works in the true market, not how well the generator matches stylized facts. A listed GitHub path in the paper did not fetch this morning; the arXiv abstract did.

stories.hed: Nvidia customers told AI-server prices are rising more than 15%

grafs: Some of Nvidia’s biggest customers have been told that prices of servers containing its AI chips are, in many cases, going up by more than 15 percent, Bloomberg reported Saturday, as recapped by The Straits Times. The increases would take effect on systems shipped in early 2027, including those with Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell chips, people familiar with the process said.

Contract manufacturers that build the servers for large data-centre operators, including Microsoft, Google and Oracle, have recently notified customers, the sources said. The increases will depend on the generation of Nvidia chips and the memory configuration. Memory costs — Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron — are the driver. Nvidia representatives did not respond to requests for comment.

The more-than-15-percent figure is a report from people familiar with private communications, not a number Nvidia has published. Do not treat it as a company print. The company reports Wednesday, Aug. 26.

stories.hed: Lean Marketron: 18 parameters down to 9
stories.dek: Itkin, NYU Tandon. arXiv 2608.20589. Monday q-fin. Gauge-fix the inelastic marketron so flow risk is identifiable.
stories.action: Read the 9-parameter core and the market-price-of-flow-risk wedge. Do not recalibrate the 18.
grafs: Andrey Itkin of NYU Tandon posted “Calibrating Inelastic Markets to Options: The Lean Marketron and the Generalized Langevin Equation” to arXiv (2608.20589) on the q-fin list. The Marketron model and its option-pricing extension suffered from structural non-identifiability: an 18-parameter space trapped solvers in local minima.

By removing exact scaling gauges and sign symmetries, freezing non-financial parameters, and adiabatically eliminating the fast hidden signal, he derives a nine-parameter reduced model. A Gauss-Newton Hessian with empty null space and a manifold-boundary analysis confirm that the reduced core carries no exact symmetry and admits no further reduction.

A staged calibration from the physical measure to the risk-neutral measure, illustrated on SPX options, fits the whole surface with a single parameter set. The wedge between physical and pricing values of the flow block becomes a well-defined market price of flow risk rather than a ridge artifact.

stories.hed: Deep hedging: compatibility, not fidelity
stories.dek: Hashimoto, Hirano, Ozaki, Imajo. arXiv 2608.20842. The gap that matters is whether the strategy still works in the true market.
stories.action: Score generators on the compatibility gap, not stylized-fact RMSE.
grafs: Ryuji Hashimoto, Masanori Hirano, Ryota Ozaki and Kentaro Imajo (University of Tokyo and Preferred Networks) posted “Rethinking Synthetic Scenario Realism: Compatibility, Not Fidelity, Drives Hedging Performance” to arXiv (2608.20842).

Deep hedging trains on synthetic paths because real market data is scarce. The literature scores generators on realism — how well they match stylized facts. The authors define compatibility as whether a strategy trained on the synthetic measure still works in the true market. Hedging performance decomposes into learning error and a compatibility gap; realism and compatibility can diverge.

Empirically, performance is governed by alignment between generator and hedger, plus task structure — path dependence, transaction costs — not by realism alone. Rankings of generators reorder when the hedger class or the option changes.

stories.hed: Ant FalconTST 2.0 is in G-SIB FX books

grafs: Ant International released Falcon Time-Series Transformer 2.0 for cash-flow and FX exposure on cross-border payments. The company said the model scored 0.666 MASE on a public time-series foundation-model benchmark, at the top of that leaderboard, and has held forecast accuracy above 93 percent.

Kelvin Li, general manager of platform tech, said 2.0 is how the firm extends the 1.0 cost save to bank partners and to e-commerce, travel and fintech. An API trial is on GitHub; the technical report is arXiv 2608.13262.

stories.hed: BOCHK and Ant put AI on the treasury wire
stories.dek: Alipay+ settlement in Southeast Asia, Bettr on-chain cash, WorldFirst for SMEs. FX pricing plus Ant models.
stories.action: Map Alipay+ / Bettr / WorldFirst against a PE portco treasury stack: settlement bank, FX, SME cash.
grafs: Bank of China (Hong Kong) and Ant International, partners since 2013, announced a strategic tie-up for cross-border payments, real-time treasury and SME cash. The bank’s FX book is meant to sit next to Ant’s models.

Three Ant rails are named. BOCHK will supply accounts and settlement banking so Alipay+ can clear across Southeast Asia. Bettr will work with the bank on distributed-ledger and tokenised cash and investment tools. WorldFirst will package cross-border fund management for SMEs, including Chinese firms going out.

BOCHK customers can already link accounts and cards to AlipayHK for transfers, payments and top-ups. Sun Yu, vice-chairman and chief executive of BOCHK, and Eric Jing, Ant International chairman, signed the release.

stories.hed: Broadcom shops a $60B-plus AI chip financing
stories.dek: Talks, not a close. Blackstone and Apollo. A $35B Anthropic package is already on the page.

A junior piece of about $30 billion and a senior-secured tranche of about $60 billion to $70 billion, with Broadcom guaranteeing part of the senior, could take the package toward $100 billion. The debt would sit in a special-purpose vehicle.

Blackstone declined to comment. Broadcom and Apollo did not immediately respond, Reuters said. It remains a talk, not a close — the same test as the Nvidia $500 billion capacity platforms.

stories.hed: Rillet Raises $100M Series C at $1B to Build Accounting Superintelligence

grafs: Rillet, the AI-native enterprise resource planning company, has raised $100 million in a Series C led by ICONIQ at a $1 billion valuation, with Sequoia and Andreessen Horowitz participating. The round is the firm’s third in about 12 months.

The company now lists more than 600 customers and says it doubled new annual recurring revenue in the last three months. It is pitching a replacement of Oracle Fusion, SAP, Workday, Microsoft Dynamics GP and NetSuite. Named customers include Mercor — said to run past $2 billion in ARR with a three-person finance team — Function Health and Temporal.
An alliance with EY is live in 2026. Fortune published an exclusive, now paywalled, on the unicorn round and chief executive Nicolas Kopp.

stories.hed: Stripe agrees to acquire OpenRouter
stories.dek: Tokens as the central currency: the payments firm wants both sides of the ledger — revenue and token cost.
stories.action: Treat as a CFO / FinOps buying signal: who owns AI inference spend, who is on OpenRouter vs building a router.
grafs: Stripe has agreed to acquire OpenRouter, a gateway that routes inference across more than 400 models from more than 80 providers. The payments company said tokens are the central currency for firms building with AI, and that it wants both sides of the ledger: revenue and token cost.
OpenRouter is already used by NVIDIA, Zoom and Lovable. Together, Stripe said, the two would help businesses maximize revenue while routing requests to the right model at the right price.
The New York Times, via Payments Dive, put the price at $7.5 billion, including $1.5 billion to the founders. Stripe declined to confirm. The figure remains unconfirmed and is behind a paywall.

stories.hed: Snowflake Cortex adds dynamic model routing
stories.dek: The gateway auto-picks the cheapest approved model, inside audit and residency controls already on the warehouse.
stories.action: Compare routing + audit / residency vs OpenRouter / Stripe.
grafs: Snowflake is adding dynamic model routing to Cortex AI Gateway, a capability the company said will enter private preview soon. The gateway auto-picks the cheapest approved model for a given task, and only from the set an administrator has already allowed.

In internal tests, routing delivered up to three times the token efficiency on a dbt pipeline versus a frontier-model-only approach, and about 25 percent fewer tokens on pull-request work, Snowflake said.

Each routing decision is logged and stays inside existing data-residency settings. The comparison for finance desks is routing plus audit and residency versus a public gateway such as OpenRouter, now heading into Stripe.

stories.hed: Workday stands up an AI Research team
stories.dek: Same day as the Rillet raise. The brief is audit trail and forgetting, not chat UX.
stories.action: Pair with Rillet: audit trail and forgetting, not chat UX.
grafs: Workday introduced an AI Research team on the same day as the Rillet raise, dedicated to reliable, trustworthy and efficient enterprise AI. The work is aimed at what an agent keeps, what it can explain, and whether a delete is in fact a delete.

A selective agent-memory method delivered 12 percent higher precision and about 8 percent better memory quality, while retaining 97 percent of useful memories and running about 31 percent faster, the company said. Splitting work across specialized agents improved accuracy by 5.8 percent.

When researchers asked an agent to forget, a recoverable copy remained about one in five times. Fully erasing required deleting every summary that mentioned the item. Workday is also funding a $50,000-a-year PhD fellowship.

stories.hed: What Makes a Peer? Valuation-Anchored Similarity in Private Markets
stories.dek: BlackRock trains CatBoost on ~53,000 post-money valuations. Similarity is leaf co-occurrence, not SIC or embeddings.
stories.action: Read method and k-NN tables; implementable comps infra.
grafs: BlackRock researchers have posted a method for finding private-market peers that starts from valuation, not industry codes. The paper, dated Aug. 12, trains CatBoost on about 53,000 post-money valuations in a universe of about 270,000 private companies.

Similarity is defined as importance-weighted leaf co-occurrence across the ensemble — firms that land in the same trees, weighted by how much those trees matter — rather than SIC or NAICS codes or text embeddings. The metric beat Euclidean, Gower and embedding distances on k-nearest-neighbor valuation tasks in the groups tested.
SHAP attributions show deal type and country dominate the valuation drivers, and therefore the peer map. The k-NN tables are the implementable comps infrastructure.

The valuation engine refuses missing DCF inputs rather than emitting a silent number. A private-equity cash-flow spine adds XIRR, MOIC, DPI and TVPI. The MCP surface has grown to 74 tools.

stories.hed: Nvidia and the $500B compute capital
stories.dek: Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman and KKR. Capacity, not cash in the door. Still live this week.
stories.action: 10-Q MD&A confirms MOUs to mobilize more than $500 billion and optional limited residual-value support, without naming the six. Names remain Aug. 10 IR only. Do not collapse with the signed $105B SB Energy cap (nvda-10q). Still: first real facility — term sheet, not MOU.
grafs: Nvidia has lined up more than $500 billion of compute capital with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR, in a structure announced Aug. 10 and still live this week. The figure is capacity, not cash in the door.
The memorandums of understanding treat Nvidia compute as an investable asset class — infrastructure that can be underwritten, not a vendor-financing footnote.

Chief executive Jensen Huang said Nvidia may backstop up to 25 percent of an opportunity, or about $125 billion. The live question is which platform is first to a real customer facility — a term sheet, not an MOU.

stories.hed: AI Premium
stories.dek: 380 trillion tokens, 400+ models. High-AI-beta stocks outperformed low by 64.1 bp a week. The meter is OpenRouter.
stories.action: Frame Stripe–OpenRouter as buying the meter the academy used to price AI risk.
grafs: A National Bureau of Economic Research paper, posted in HTML on arXiv on Aug. 11, prices AI the way a desk prices any other factor. Using 380 trillion tokens across more than 400 models from January 2024 through April 2026, the authors construct an AI factor from growth in tokens, dollars and users.
Stocks with high AI betas outperformed low-beta names by 64.1 basis points a week on a value-weighted basis (t = 2.84). The premium loads on intensive, frontier use, not casual traffic.

The agentic share of tokens rose from about zero in 2024 to 52.2 percent. The data come from OpenRouter. Stripe’s bid for that gateway is a bid for the meter the academy used to price the risk. The NBER PDF may be gated; the arXiv HTML is not.
